test_title: SSC MTS 2023 Official Paper (Held On: 04 Sept, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
The given sentence contains an error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error.

That career competition was the difficultest exam he had ever given.

options.text: That career competition was the difficultest exam than any he had ever given.
That career competition was the most difficult exam than any he had ever given.
That career competition was the most difficultest exam he had ever given.
That career competition was the most difficult exam he had ever given.

solution:
The correct answer is '**That career competition was the most difficult exam he had ever given**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word "**difficultest**" is incorrect. The correct superlative form of "**difficult**" is "**most difficult**."
 
• The sentence should use "**the most difficult**" instead of "**the difficultest**."
 
• **Option 4** correctly uses "**most difficult**" to form the superlative degree.
 
• The phrase "**had ever given**" is correctly placed and does not need any changes.

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

Correct sentence: *That career competition was the most difficult exam he had ever given*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "That career competition was the difficultest exam than any he had ever given." - This option incorrectly uses "difficultest" and awkwardly structures the comparison.
 
• **Option 2:** "That career competition was the most difficult exam than any he had ever given." - This option correctly uses "most difficult," but the phrase "than any" is redundant and incorrect.
 
• **Option 3:** "That career competition was the most difficultest exam he had ever given." - This option incorrectly combines "most" and "difficultest," which is grammatically incorrect.
